title: Factorization criterion for henselian pairs
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Then $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] (for every finite $A$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/IB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$) if and only if (i) $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and (ii) for every monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and every factorization $\overline f=g_0h_0$ of its reduction $\overline f\in(A/I)[T]$ into monic polynomials $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[T]$ generating the unit ideal of $(A/I)[T]$, there are monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ whose reductions modulo $I$ are $g_0$ and $h_0$. In particular, if $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, then $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if (ii) holds.

proof.text: The recorded henselian predicate is Mathlib HenselianRing A I. Its jac field gives I ≤ jacobson(0) directly.

For monic f set B = AdjoinRoot f, a finite A-algebra by Polynomial.Monic.finite_adjoinRoot. Choose Bezout coefficients a,b for g0,h0. The element p0=b*h0 has residues 1 and 0 in the two factor quotients and is idempotent modulo f0=g0*h0. Lift p0 to a polynomial p using surjectivity of coefficient reduction. AdjoinRoot.quotAdjoinRootEquivQuotPolynomialQuot identifies its class in B/IB with this idempotent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-integral-idempotent-lifting] to get an idempotent e of B. Factor the maps to AdjoinRoot g0 and AdjoinRoot h0 through B/IB; applying them to the lifted equality gives residues 1 and 0. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-splitting-monic-factorization] to obtain the required factors. All quotient and Bezout glue is proved in the private helper factorization_of_lifting.

proof.text: Conversely assume the Jacobson condition and monic coprime factorization lifting. To prove the is_henselian field, take monic f and a0 with f(a0) in I and f'(a0) a unit modulo I. Handle the zero ring by nontriviality. In a nonzero ring the Jacobson condition implies I is proper, so A/I is nonzero. Put x=a0 mod I and f0=f mod I. Divide f0 by X-C(x); since f0(x)=0 the remainder vanishes and f0=(X-C(x))*q with q monic. The differentiated division identity gives q(x)=f0'(x), a unit. Dividing q by X-C(x) and multiplying its remainder identity by q(x)^(-1) provides explicit Bezout coefficients, proving IsCoprime (X-C(x)) q. Lift this factorization to f=g*h. Reduction preserves the degree of monic g, so g has degree one. Thus g=X+C(g.coeff 0), and alpha=-g.coeff 0 is a root of f. Taking constant coefficients of g mod I=X-C(x) proves alpha-a0 in I. This establishes Mathlib HenselianRing without any additional assumption.
